guard.negative_proof: tests/architecture/build-stamp.test.mjs: checkStamp() refuses a stamp from another commit and a missing stamp; disabling the commit comparison turns the test red. 2026-10-21: with a decoy server on 127.0.0.1:3000, `playwright test` refuses to start ("is already used", exit 1); the architecture test rejects !process.env.CI, true and an unset value. 2026-10-24: a global-setup that returns early when PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_URL is set fails tests/architecture/local-server-isolation.test.mjs (remote base URL no longer refused); checkLaneURL rejects remote, lookalike (127.0.0.1.evil.example), private-IP and malformed URLs; checkServedCommit rejects a missing or foreign served commit.
guard.path: tests/e2e/build-stamp.mjs (checkStamp) + tests/e2e/global-setup.mjs (loopback-only lane, stamp check with PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_URL set, served-commit check) + astro.config.mjs buildStamp integration + playwright.config.ts webServer.reuseExistingServer: false (tests/architecture/local-server-isolation.test.mjs)

recurrences.evidence: Twice in the 2026-10-20/21 wave: a local run for PR #649 and one for PR #645 tested another worktree's build through an astro preview left on port 3000 (reuseExistingServer: !CI). The #645 run showed 22 false failures; rerun on its own build, 136 passed.
recurrences.guard_root_cause: The stamp check compares the local dist/ to HEAD, but Playwright then reused whatever server already answered on port 3000, so the build under test was never the one that was checked.
recurrences.reason_if_not: Already G3 (preflight). G4 is an SGPS portable guard and not this project's to ship; the guard is widened at G3 instead: playwright.config.ts sets reuseExistingServer: false and tests/architecture/local-server-isolation.test.mjs pins it. Flagged to the control plane as a portable candidate.

recurrences.evidence: Three parallel lanes ran Playwright with PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:<port> against their own astro preview. That skips webServer; one lane reported the webServer step was bypassed. The run was therefore tied to no checked build: nothing verified that the server on the URL served this worktree's HEAD, and a remote URL was equally accepted.
recurrences.guard_root_cause: The guard verified the local dist/ stamp and the webServer port, never the server the browser actually talked to. A base URL pointing at any host (or at another worktree's loopback preview) was outside the guard's reach.
recurrences.reason_if_not: Already G3 (preflight). G4 is an SGPS portable guard and not this project's to ship; the guard is widened at G3 instead: global-setup now refuses a non-loopback PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_URL, still runs checkStamp when the base URL is set, and compares the commit served at /.well-known/build-commit with HEAD (tests/architecture/local-server-isolation.test.mjs, build-stamp.test.mjs). Flagged to the control plane as a portable candidate.

reuse_boundary: Local development only. CI builds fresh, so the check is a no-op there (guarded by !process.env.CI). Known gaps: uncommitted edits on the same HEAD are not detected, and the run is allowed when git is unavailable. The served-build check runs only when this worktree's dist/ carries .well-known/build-commit (written by local builds, never by CI or Workers Builds); otherwise only the local stamp is verified. A non-loopback PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_URL is refused for local runs by design. The stamp lives in .astro/ (git-ignored), never in the deployed dist/.
root_cause: Local Playwright runs served dist/ via `astro preview` with no check that dist/ matched HEAD. A stale build produced failures unrelated to the working tree.
rule: Local Playwright runs only against a dist/ built from the current HEAD. A build stamp (.astro/build-commit) is compared to `git rev-parse HEAD` in a local-only globalSetup; mismatch refuses the run. Playwright never reuses an existing server on the port.
title: Local Playwright must refuse a stale dist/ build
trigger: 2026-10-16: local e2e was falsely red twice on a stale dist/ (built from an older HEAD than the working tree).
